chapters.title: The Ark Brought to Jerusalem
chapters.html:
1 Chronicles 15

The Levites Prepare

1David made houses for himself in the City of David, and he prepared a place for the ark of God and pitched a tent for it.

2Then David said, "No one but the Levites may carry the ark of God, for the LORD chose them to carry the ark of the LORD and to minister to Him forever."

3David assembled all Israel at Jerusalem to bring up the ark of the LORD to its place, which he had prepared for it.

4David gathered the sons of Aaron and the Levites:

5of the sons of Kohath, Uriel the chief, with a hundred and twenty of his kinsmen;

6of the sons of Merari, Asaiah the chief, with two hundred and twenty of his kinsmen;

7of the sons of Gershom, Joel the chief, with a hundred and thirty of his kinsmen;

8of the sons of Elizaphan, Shemaiah the chief, with two hundred of his kinsmen;

9of the sons of Hebron, Eliel the chief, with eighty of his kinsmen;

10of the sons of Uzziel, Amminadab the chief, with a hundred and twelve of his kinsmen.

11David called Zadok and Abiathar the priests, and the Levites Uriel, Asaiah, Joel, Shemaiah, Eliel and Amminadab,

12and said to them, "You are the heads of the fathers' houses of the Levites. Consecrate yourselves, you and your kinsmen, and bring up the ark of the LORD, the God of Israel, to the place I have prepared for it.

13Because you did not carry it the first time, the LORD our God broke out against us, for we did not seek Him according to the rule."

14So the priests and the Levites consecrated themselves to bring up the ark of the LORD, the God of Israel.

15The sons of the Levites carried the ark of God on their shoulders with the poles on them, as Moses had commanded according to the word of the LORD.

The Singers

16David told the chiefs of the Levites to appoint their kinsmen as the singers, with instruments of music, harps, lyres and cymbals, to play loudly and to raise sounds of joy.

17So the Levites appointed Heman son of Joel; and of his kinsmen, Asaph son of Berechiah; and of the sons of Merari their kinsmen, Ethan son of Kushaiah;

18and with them their kinsmen of the second rank: Zechariah, Jaaziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, Obed-edom and Jeiel, the gatekeepers.

19The singers Heman, Asaph and Ethan were to sound bronze cymbals;

20Zechariah, Aziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Maaseiah and Benaiah, with harps according to Alamoth;

21and Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, Obed-edom, Jeiel and Azaziah, to lead with lyres according to the Sheminith.

22Chenaniah, chief of the Levites, was in charge of the carrying; he directed the carrying, for he understood it.

23Berechiah and Elkanah were gatekeepers for the ark.

24Shebaniah, Joshaphat, Nethanel, Amasai, Zechariah, Benaiah and Eliezer the priests blew the trumpets before the ark of God. Obed-edom and Jehiah were gatekeepers for the ark.

The Ark Comes In

25So David and the elders of Israel and the commanders of thousands went to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD from the house of Obed-edom with joy.

26Because God helped the Levites who carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD, they sacrificed seven bulls and seven rams.

27David was clothed in a robe of fine linen, as were all the Levites who carried the ark, the singers, and Chenaniah the leader of the carrying of the singers; and David wore a linen ephod.

28So all Israel brought up the ark of the covenant of the LORD with shouting, with the sound of the horn, with trumpets and cymbals, playing loudly on harps and lyres.

29As the ark of the covenant of the LORD came to the City of David, Michal the daughter of Saul looked down through the window and saw King David dancing and celebrating, and she despised him in her heart.

Notes

  • v2 "No one but the Levites may carry the ark of God" — the law: At that time the LORD set apart the tribe of Levi to carry the ark of the covenant of the LORD (Deuteronomy 10:8). The first attempt used a cart (13:7).

  • v13 "the LORD our God broke out against us, for we did not seek Him according to the rule" — parats, the breach of Perez-uzza (13:11), and lo derashnuhu ka-mishpat. Chronicles names the cause Samuel leaves unsaid: the ark was not carried as the law says.

  • v15 "on their shoulders with the poles on them, as Moses had commanded" — You shall put the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark, to carry the ark by them (Exodus 25:14); the sons of Kohath carried on their shoulders (Numbers 7:9).

  • v18 "Zechariah, Jaaziel" — the Hebrew has Zechariah ben, Jaaziel, with ben, son of, and no name after it. The Greek lacks the word, and the same list in v20 runs Zechariah, Aziel without it. The text follows the Greek.

  • vv20–21 "according to Alamoth… according to the Sheminith" — al alamot, al ha-sheminit, terms found in the headings of the Psalms: according to Alamoth (Psalm 46), according to the Sheminith (Psalms 6 and 12). Alamot is the word for young women, sheminit the eighth; what they meant in music is not known.

  • vv22, 27 "in charge of the carrying… the leader of the carrying of the singers" — massa, lifting, carrying, from the verb of v2 (la-set, to carry), or lifting up of the voice in song. The Greek has chief of the songs. Uncertain; the text keeps carrying, the word of the chapter.

  • v26 "seven bulls and seven rams" — Samuel has an ox and a fatted calf when the bearers had gone six steps (2 Samuel 6:13). Because God helped the Levites: this time the ark is carried, and no one dies.

  • v27 "a robe of fine linen… a linen ephod" — me'il buts and efod bad. Samuel has only the linen ephod (2 Samuel 6:14).

  • v29 "Michal the daughter of Saul… despised him in her heart" — as in 2 Samuel 6:16, but Chronicles stops there, without the words between Michal and David (2 Samuel 6:20–23). Samuel has David leaping and dancing, mefazzez u-mekharker; Chronicles dancing and celebrating, meraqqed u-mesacheq.

chapters.title: The Ark in Its Tent and David's Song of Thanks
chapters.html:
1 Chronicles 16

The Ark Set in the Tent

1They brought in the ark of God and set it inside the tent that David had pitched for it, and they offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before God.

2When David had finished offering the burnt offerings and the peace offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD.

3He distributed to all Israel, both men and women, to each a loaf of bread, a portion of meat and a cake of raisins.

4He appointed some of the Levites as ministers before the ark of the LORD, to bring to remembrance, to thank and to praise the LORD, the God of Israel:

5Asaph the chief, and second to him Zechariah, then Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-edom and Jeiel, with harps and lyres; Asaph was to sound the cymbals,

6and Benaiah and Jahaziel the priests were to blow trumpets continually before the ark of the covenant of God.

The Song of Thanks

7On that day David first appointed that thanks be given to the LORD by Asaph and his kinsmen:

8Give thanks to the LORD, call on His name;
make known His deeds among the peoples.

9Sing to Him, sing praises to Him;
tell of all His wonders.

10Glory in His holy name;
let the hearts of those who seek the LORD rejoice.

11Seek the LORD and His strength;
seek His face continually.

12Remember the wonders He has done,
His signs and the judgments of His mouth,

13O seed of Israel His servant,
sons of Jacob, His chosen ones!

14He is the LORD our God;
His judgments are in all the earth.

15Remember His covenant forever,
the word He commanded for a thousand generations,

16the covenant He made with Abraham,
His oath to Isaac,

17which He confirmed to Jacob as a statute,
to Israel as an everlasting covenant,

18saying, "To you I will give the land of Canaan
as the portion of your inheritance,"

19when you were few in number,
very few, and guests in it,

20and they wandered from nation to nation,
from one kingdom to another people.

21He allowed no one to oppress them;
He rebuked kings on their account:

22"Do not touch My anointed ones,
and do My prophets no harm."

23Sing to the LORD, all the earth;
proclaim His salvation from day to day.

24Declare His glory among the nations,
His wonders among all the peoples.

25For great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised;
He is to be feared above all gods.

26For all the gods of the peoples are idols,
but the LORD made the heavens.

27Splendor and majesty are before Him;
strength and joy are in His place.

28Ascribe to the LORD, O families of the peoples,
ascribe to the LORD glory and strength.

29Ascribe to the LORD the glory of His name;
bring an offering and come before Him.
Worship the LORD in the splendor of holiness;

30tremble before Him, all the earth.
The world is established; it shall not be moved.

31Let the heavens be glad, and let the earth rejoice,
and let them say among the nations, "The LORD reigns!"

32Let the sea roar, and all that fills it;
let the field exult, and all that is in it.

33Then the trees of the forest will sing for joy before the LORD,
for He comes to judge the earth.

34Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good,
for His loyal love endures forever.

35Say also:
"Save us, O God of our salvation,
gather us and deliver us from the nations,
to give thanks to Your holy name
and to glory in Your praise.

36Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel,
from everlasting to everlasting!"
Then all the people said "Amen" and praised the LORD.

The Service Arranged

37So David left Asaph and his kinsmen there before the ark of the covenant of the LORD to minister before the ark continually, as each day required,

38and Obed-edom and their kinsmen, sixty-eight; Obed-edom son of Jeduthun and Hosah were to be gatekeepers.

39He left Zadok the priest and his kinsmen the priests before the dwelling of the LORD at the high place that was at Gibeon,

40to offer burnt offerings to the LORD on the altar of burnt offering continually, morning and evening, according to all that is written in the instruction of the LORD that He commanded Israel.

41With them were Heman and Jeduthun and the rest of those chosen and designated by name to give thanks to the LORD, for His loyal love endures forever.

42Heman and Jeduthun had with them trumpets and cymbals for those who were to sound them, and the instruments for the songs of God. The sons of Jeduthun were to be at the gate.

43Then all the people went away, each to his house, and David returned to bless his household.

Notes

  • vv8–36 and the Psalms — David's song is made of three psalms: vv8–22 are Psalm 105:1–15, vv23–33 most of Psalm 96, and vv34–36 the opening and closing lines of Psalm 106 (106:1, 47–48).

  • v4 "to bring to remembrance, to thank and to praise" — le-hazkir, the word in the headings of Psalms 38 and 70, to bring to remembrance.

  • v13 "O seed of Israel His servant" — Psalm 105:6 has O seed of Abraham His servant.

  • v15 "Remember His covenant forever" — Psalm 105:8 has He has remembered His covenant forever, of God; here the people are told to remember it. In v19 Chronicles has when you were few in number where the psalm has when they were few (Psalm 105:12).

  • v19 "very few, and guests in it" — gerim, fixed as guests: the patriarchs living in Canaan without owning it.

  • v22 "Do not touch My anointed ones, and do My prophets no harm" — meshichai, My anointed ones, said of the patriarchs; Abraham is called a prophet (Genesis 20:7).

  • v27 "strength and joy are in His place" — Psalm 96:6 has strength and beauty are in His sanctuary. In David's day there is no sanctuary yet; the ark stands in a tent.

  • v35 "gather us and deliver us from the nations" — the last lines of Psalm 106 (106:47), a prayer of exiles, in David's song at the ark's coming.

  • vv34, 41 "for His loyal love endures forever" — ki le-olam chasdo, chesed, fixed as loyal love: the refrain of Psalms 106 and 136 and the words the singers are appointed to say (v41).

  • vv37–42 "before the ark… before the dwelling of the LORD at the high place that was at Gibeon" — two places of worship: the ark in its tent in Jerusalem with Asaph's singers, and the dwelling of Moses with the altar of burnt offering at Gibeon with Zadok. Chronicles names Gibeon again where Solomon goes to sacrifice, for the tent of meeting of God was there (2 Chronicles 1:3).

chapters.title: The LORD's Promise to David
chapters.html:
1 Chronicles 17

Nathan's Word

1And it came to pass, when David lived in his house, that David said to Nathan the prophet, "See now, I live in a house of cedar, but the ark of the covenant of the LORD stays under curtains."

2Nathan said to David, "Do all that is in your heart, for God is with you."

3And it came to pass that same night that the word of God came to Nathan, saying,

4"Go and tell My servant David, 'Thus says the LORD: You shall not build Me the house to dwell in.

5For I have not lived in a house from the day I brought up Israel to this day, but I have gone from tent to tent and from dwelling to dwelling.

6Wherever I have moved about among all Israel, did I ever speak a word to any of the judges of Israel whom I commanded to shepherd My people, saying, "Why have you not built Me a house of cedar?"'

7Now then, say this to My servant David: 'Thus says the LORD of hosts: I took you from the pasture, from following the sheep, to be leader over My people Israel.

8I have been with you wherever you went and have cut off all your enemies before you. I will make you a name like the name of the great ones on the earth.

9I will appoint a place for My people Israel and will plant them, so that they may dwell in their own place and be disturbed no more. The wicked shall wear them down no more as at first,

10from the days I commanded judges over My people Israel. I will subdue all your enemies. I declare to you that the LORD will build you a house.

11And it shall come to pass, when your days are fulfilled to go to be with your fathers, that I will raise up your seed after you, one of your own sons, and I will establish his kingdom.

12He shall build Me a house, and I will establish his throne forever.

13I will be his father, and he shall be My son. I will not take My loyal love away from him, as I took it from him who was before you.

14I will set him over My house and over My kingdom forever, and his throne shall be established forever.'"

15In accordance with all these words and all this vision, so Nathan spoke to David.

David's Prayer

16Then King David went in and sat before the LORD and said, "Who am I, O LORD God, and what is my house, that You have brought me this far?

17Yet this was too small in Your eyes, O God; You have spoken of Your servant's house for a long time to come, and You have regarded me as a man of high rank, O LORD God.

18What more can David say to You for the honor shown to Your servant? For You know Your servant.

19O LORD, for Your servant's sake and according to Your own heart, You have done all this greatness, to make known all these great things.

20O LORD, there is none like You, and there is no God besides You, according to all that we have heard with our ears.

21Who is like Your people Israel, the one nation on earth whom God went to redeem as a people for Himself, to make for Yourself a name by great and awesome things, by driving out nations before Your people whom You redeemed from Egypt?

22You made Your people Israel Your own people forever, and You, O LORD, became their God.

23So now, O LORD, let the word You have spoken concerning Your servant and concerning his house be made sure forever, and do as You have spoken.

24Let it be made sure, and let Your name be great forever, saying, 'The LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, is Israel's God,' and let the house of David Your servant be established before You.

25For You, my God, have revealed to Your servant that You will build him a house. That is why Your servant has found courage to pray before You.

26So now, O LORD, You are God, and You have promised this good thing to Your servant.

27So now, You have been pleased to bless the house of Your servant, that it may continue forever before You. For You, O LORD, have blessed it, and it is blessed forever."

Notes

  • vv1–27 and 2 Samuel 7 — the same chapter, with changes small and large. Chronicles leaves out the LORD had given him rest from all his enemies (2 Samuel 7:1).

  • v4 "You shall not build Me the house" — a statement; Samuel has a question, Will you build Me a house to dwell in? (2 Samuel 7:5). The Greek of Samuel agrees with Chronicles.

  • v5 "from tent to tent and from dwelling to dwelling" — the Hebrew breaks off, from tent to tent and from dwelling; to dwelling is supplied from the sense. Samuel has moving about in a tent for My dwelling (2 Samuel 7:6).

  • v6 "any of the judges of Israel" — shoftei, judges; Samuel has shivtei, tribes (2 Samuel 7:7). The two words differ in one letter, and judges is what v10 also has.

  • v13 "I will be his father, and he shall be My son" — Samuel goes on, When he does wrong, I will discipline him with the rod of men (2 Samuel 7:14); Chronicles has no such words. Saul is not named either: him who was before you. Hebrews applies the promise to Jesus: I will be a Father to Him, and He shall be a Son to Me (Hebrews 1:5).

  • v14 "I will set him over My house and over My kingdom forever" — Samuel has your house and your kingdom (2 Samuel 7:16). In Chronicles the house and the kingdom are the LORD's, and David's son is set over them.

  • vv16–17 "O LORD God… O God… O LORD God" — YHWH Elohim and Elohim, where Samuel's prayer has Adonai YHWH, Lord GOD, throughout.

  • v17 "You have regarded me as a man of high rank" — u-re'itani ke-tor ha-adam ha-ma'alah, You have seen me according to the manner of a man of ascent; the sense is uncertain. Samuel has this is the instruction for mankind (2 Samuel 7:19). The text keeps the Hebrew of each.

  • v25 "You, my God, have revealed to Your servant" — galita et ozen avdekha, You have uncovered the ear of Your servant, the same words as the LORD had revealed to Samuel the day before Saul came (1 Samuel 9:15).

  • v27 "For You, O LORD, have blessed it, and it is blessed forever" — Samuel ends with a request, with Your blessing let the house of Your servant be blessed forever; Chronicles ends with the blessing already given.

Nathan's Word

Nathan said to David, "Do all that is in your heart, for God is with you."
And it came to pass that same night that the word of God came to Nathan, saying,
"Go and tell My servant David, 'Thus says the LORD: You shall not build Me the house to dwell in.
For I have not lived in a house from the day I brought up Israel to this day, but I have gone from tent to tent and from dwelling to dwelling.
Wherever I have moved about among all Israel, did I ever speak a word to any of the judges of Israel whom I commanded to shepherd My people, saying, "Why have you not built Me a house of cedar?"'
Now then, say this to My servant David: 'Thus says the LORD of hosts: I took you from the pasture, from following the sheep, to be leader over My people Israel.
I have been with you wherever you went and have cut off all your enemies before you. I will make you a name like the name of the great ones on the earth.
I will appoint a place for My people Israel and will plant them, so that they may dwell in their own place and be disturbed no more. The wicked shall wear them down no more as at first,
from the days I commanded judges over My people Israel. I will subdue all your enemies. I declare to you that the LORD will build you a house.
And it shall come to pass, when your days are fulfilled to go to be with your fathers, that I will raise up your seed after you, one of your own sons, and I will establish his kingdom.
He shall build Me a house, and I will establish his throne forever.
I will be his father, and he shall be My son. I will not take My loyal love away from him, as I took it from him who was before you.
I will set him over My house and over My kingdom forever, and his throne shall be established forever.'"

O LORD, there is none like You, and there is no God besides You, according to all that we have heard with our ears.

Who is like Your people Israel, the one nation on earth whom God went to redeem as a people for Himself, to make for Yourself a name by great and awesome things, by driving out nations before Your people whom You redeemed from Egypt?
You made Your people Israel Your own people forever, and You, O LORD, became their God.

Let it be made sure, and let Your name be great forever, saying, 'The LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, is Israel's God,' and let the house of David Your servant be established before You.

So now, O LORD, You are God, and You have promised this good thing to Your servant.
So now, You have been pleased to bless the house of Your servant, that it may continue forever before You. For You, O LORD, have blessed it, and it is blessed forever."

chapters.title: David's Wars and Officials
chapters.html:
1 Chronicles 18

David's Victories

1And it came to pass after this that David struck the Philistines and subdued them, and he took Gath and its villages out of the hand of the Philistines.

2He struck Moab, and the Moabites became David's servants and brought tribute.

3David also struck Hadadezer king of Zobah, toward Hamath, as he went to set up his monument at the river Euphrates.

4David captured from him a thousand chariots, seven thousand horsemen and twenty thousand foot soldiers. David hamstrung all the chariot horses, but left enough of them for a hundred chariots.

5When the Arameans of Damascus came to help Hadadezer king of Zobah, David struck twenty-two thousand men of the Arameans.

6Then David put garrisons in Aram of Damascus, and the Arameans became David's servants and brought tribute. The LORD gave David victory wherever he went.

7David took the shields of gold that were on the servants of Hadadezer and brought them to Jerusalem.

8From Tibhath and from Cun, towns of Hadadezer, David took a great quantity of bronze. With it Solomon made the bronze Sea, the pillars and the vessels of bronze.

9When Tou king of Hamath heard that David had struck the whole army of Hadadezer king of Zobah,

10he sent Hadoram his son to King David to greet him and to bless him, because he had fought against Hadadezer and struck him, for Hadadezer had been at war with Tou. He brought all kinds of articles of gold, of silver and of bronze.

11These also King David dedicated to the LORD, together with the silver and the gold that he had carried off from all the nations: from Edom, from Moab, from the sons of Ammon, from the Philistines and from Amalek.

12Abishai son of Zeruiah struck down eighteen thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt.

13He put garrisons in Edom, and all the Edomites became David's servants. The LORD gave David victory wherever he went.

David's Officials

14So David reigned over all Israel, and he did justice and righteousness for all his people.

15Joab son of Zeruiah was over the army; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was recorder;

16Zadok son of Ahitub and Abimelech son of Abiathar were priests; Shavsha was secretary;

17Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and the Pelethites; and David's sons were the chief officers at the king's side.

Notes

  • vv1–17 and 2 Samuel 8 — the same chapter. Chronicles leaves out the measuring of the Moabites with a line (2 Samuel 8:2).

  • v1 "he took Gath and its villages" — Samuel has Metheg-ammah (2 Samuel 8:1), a phrase whose meaning is uncertain; Chronicles names the Philistine city.

  • v3 "toward Hamath, as he went to set up his monument at the river Euphrates" — le-hatsiv yado, to set up his hand, the phrase used of Saul's monument at Carmel, set up a monument for himself (1 Samuel 15:12). Samuel has to restore his power, le-hashiv yado (2 Samuel 8:3).

  • v4 "a thousand chariots, seven thousand horsemen" — the reading the text of Samuel follows from the Greek (2 Samuel 8:4); here it is in the Hebrew.

  • v8 "With it Solomon made the bronze Sea, the pillars and the vessels of bronze" — not in the Hebrew of Samuel, though the Greek of Samuel has it. Samuel names the towns Betah and Berothai (2 Samuel 8:8).

  • v12 "Abishai son of Zeruiah struck down eighteen thousand Edomites" — Samuel gives the deed to David, when he returned from striking down eighteen thousand (2 Samuel 8:13), and the heading of Psalm 60 gives it to Joab, twelve thousand of Edom in the Valley of Salt.

  • v14 "he did justice and righteousness" — mishpat u-tsedaqah, as 2 Samuel 8:15.

  • vv9–10, 16 "Tou… Hadoram… Abimelech son of Abiathar… Shavsha" — Samuel has Toi, Joram, Ahimelech son of Abiathar and Seraiah (2 Samuel 8:9–10, 17).

  • v17 "David's sons were the chief officers at the king's side" — ha-rishonim le-yad ha-melekh, the first at the king's hand. Samuel has David's sons were priests, kohanim (2 Samuel 8:18). The Greek here has the first successors of the king.

chapters.title: The War with Ammon and Aram
chapters.html:
1 Chronicles 19

Hanun Shames David's Servants

1And it came to pass after this that Nahash the king of the sons of Ammon died, and his son reigned in his place.

2David said, "I will show loyal love to Hanun son of Nahash, because his father showed loyal love to me." So David sent messengers to comfort him concerning his father, and David's servants came to the land of the sons of Ammon, to Hanun, to comfort him.

3But the princes of the sons of Ammon said to Hanun, "Do you think David is honoring your father because he has sent comforters to you? Have not his servants come to you to search, to overthrow and to spy out the land?"

4So Hanun took David's servants and shaved them, cut their garments in half as far as their buttocks, and sent them away.

5Some went and told David about the men, and he sent to meet them, for the men were deeply humiliated. The king said, "Stay in Jericho until your beards grow, and then come back."

The Battle before Medeba

6When the sons of Ammon saw that they had become a stench to David, Hanun and the sons of Ammon sent a thousand talents of silver to hire chariots and horsemen from Aram-naharaim, from Aram-maacah and from Zobah.

7They hired thirty-two thousand chariots and the king of Maacah with his people, who came and camped before Medeba. The sons of Ammon gathered from their cities and came to battle.

8When David heard it, he sent Joab and all the army, the mighty men.

9The sons of Ammon came out and drew up for battle at the entrance of the city, while the kings who had come were by themselves in the open country.

10When Joab saw that the battle was set against him in front and behind, he chose some of all the chosen men of Israel and drew them up against the Arameans.

11The rest of the people he put in the hand of Abishai his brother, and they drew up against the sons of Ammon.

12He said, "If the Arameans are too strong for me, then you shall help me. But if the sons of Ammon are too strong for you, then I will help you.

13Be strong, and let us show ourselves strong for our people and for the cities of our God. The LORD will do what is good in His eyes."

14So Joab and the people who were with him drew near before the Arameans for battle, and they fled before him.

15When the sons of Ammon saw that the Arameans had fled, they also fled before Abishai his brother and went into the city. Then Joab came to Jerusalem.

The Arameans Defeated

16When the Arameans saw that they had been struck down before Israel, they sent messengers and brought out the Arameans who were beyond the River, with Shophach the commander of Hadadezer's army at their head.

17When David was told, he gathered all Israel, crossed the Jordan, came to them and drew up against them. David drew up for battle against the Arameans, and they fought with him.

18The Arameans fled before Israel, and David killed of the Arameans the men of seven thousand chariots and forty thousand foot soldiers. He also put to death Shophach the commander of the army.

19When the servants of Hadadezer saw that they had been struck down before Israel, they made peace with David and served him. So the Arameans were not willing to help the sons of Ammon any more.

Notes

  • vv1–19 and 2 Samuel 10 — the same chapter, with different numbers and names. Chronicles adds the price, a thousand talents of silver (v6), and the place, Medeba (v7).

  • v2 "I will show loyal love to Hanun son of Nahash" — chesed, fixed as loyal love. Nahash is the Ammonite who besieged Jabesh-gilead (1 Samuel 11:1–2).

  • v3 "to search, to overthrow and to spy out the land" — Samuel has the city (2 Samuel 10:3); Chronicles has the land, and puts to overthrow, ve-lahafokh, between the other two.

  • v6 "they had become a stench to David" — hitbo'ashu, the word of 2 Samuel 10:6.

  • v6 "Aram-naharaim" — Aram of the two rivers, where Abraham's servant went to find a wife for Isaac (Genesis 24:10), and the land of Cushan-rishathaim (Judges 3:8). Samuel names Beth-rehob, Zobah, Maacah and Tob (2 Samuel 10:6).

  • v7 "thirty-two thousand chariots… before Medeba" — Samuel has twenty thousand foot soldiers, a thousand men of Maacah and twelve thousand of Tob (2 Samuel 10:6), thirty-three thousand in all. Medeba lies on the plateau east of the Jordan, all the plateau of Medeba (Joshua 13:9).

  • v13 "Be strong… The LORD will do what is good in His eyes" — as 2 Samuel 10:12.

  • v16 "Shophach the commander of Hadadezer's army" — Samuel has Shobach (2 Samuel 10:16).

  • v18 "the men of seven thousand chariots and forty thousand foot soldiers" — Samuel has seven hundred chariots and forty thousand horsemen (2 Samuel 10:18). The text keeps the Hebrew of each.

  • v19 "they made peace with David and served him" — Samuel has with Israel… served them (2 Samuel 10:19).

chapters.title: Rabbah Taken and the Philistine Giants
chapters.html:
1 Chronicles 20

Rabbah Taken

1And it came to pass at the turn of the year, at the time when kings go out, that Joab led out the army and laid waste the land of the sons of Ammon, and came and besieged Rabbah. But David stayed in Jerusalem. Joab struck Rabbah and tore it down.

2David took the crown of their king from his head and found that it weighed a talent of gold, and there was a precious stone in it, and it was placed on David's head. He brought out the spoil of the city, a very great amount.

3He brought out the people who were in it and sawed them with saws, with iron picks and with saws. So David did to all the cities of the sons of Ammon. Then David and all the people returned to Jerusalem.

The Philistine Giants

4And it came to pass after this that war broke out at Gezer with the Philistines. Then Sibbecai the Hushathite struck down Sippai, who was one of the descendants of the Rephaim, and they were subdued.

5There was again war with the Philistines, and Elhanan son of Jair struck down Lahmi the brother of Goliath the Gittite, the shaft of whose spear was like a weaver's beam.

6There was again war at Gath, and there was a man of great size who had six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot, twenty-four in number. He too was descended from the Rapha.

7He taunted Israel, and Jonathan son of Shimea, David's brother, struck him down.

8These were descended from the Rapha in Gath, and they fell by the hand of David and by the hand of his servants.

Notes

  • vv1–3 and 2 Samuel 11–12 — v1 is 2 Samuel 11:1, and vv2–3 are 2 Samuel 12:30–31. Between them Samuel tells of Bathsheba and Uriah, Nathan's parable and the death of the child (2 Samuel 11:2–12:25). Chronicles tells none of it, and Joab takes Rabbah himself: Samuel's message from Joab to David, camp against the city and capture it, or I will capture the city myself (2 Samuel 12:28), is not here.

  • v1 "But David stayed in Jerusalem" — the words that in Samuel begin the story of Bathsheba (2 Samuel 11:1); here nothing follows from them.

  • v2 "the crown of their king" — malkam, which is also the name of the Ammonite god Milcom (1 Kings 11:5).

  • v3 "sawed them with saws, with iron picks and with saws" — va-yasar ba-megerah, a verb found only here; the Greek has sawed through them with saws. Samuel has va-yasem, put them to, set them to the saws (2 Samuel 12:31), a sentence of labor, and the brick kiln. The two verbs differ in one letter; the text keeps the Hebrew of each. Chronicles has saws twice where Samuel has axes.

  • vv4–8 and 2 Samuel 21:15–22 — the four giants of Samuel, three of them told here; Samuel's first, Ishbi-benob, who nearly killed David (2 Samuel 21:16–17), is not. Samuel places the first fight at Gob; Chronicles at Gezer.

  • v5 "Elhanan son of Jair struck down Lahmi the brother of Goliath" — written Ya'ur, read Ya'ir. Samuel has Elhanan son of Jaare-oregim, the Bethlehemite, struck down Goliath the Gittite (2 Samuel 21:19); 1 Samuel 17 gives Goliath to David. The text keeps the Hebrew of each, and the note on 2 Samuel 21:19 sets out the letters.

  • vv4, 6, 8 "the Rephaim… the Rapha" — ha-Refa'im in v4, ha-Rafa in vv6 and 8: the giants of old, as Og king of Bashan… was left of the remnant of the Rephaim (Deuteronomy 3:11).

  • v6 "six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot" — the Hebrew says his fingers six and six, twenty-four; the hands and feet are supplied from Samuel (2 Samuel 21:20).

chapters.title: The Census and the Threshing Floor of Ornan
chapters.html:
1 Chronicles 21

The Census

1Satan stood up against Israel and incited David to number Israel.

2So David said to Joab and to the commanders of the people, "Go, count Israel from Beersheba to Dan, and bring me word, so that I may know their number."

3But Joab said, "May the LORD add to His people a hundred times as many as they are! My lord the king, are they not all my lord's servants? Why does my lord seek this? Why should it bring guilt on Israel?"

4But the king's word prevailed against Joab. So Joab went out and went through all Israel and came back to Jerusalem.

5Joab gave David the number of the people counted: all Israel was a million one hundred thousand men who drew the sword, and Judah four hundred and seventy thousand men who drew the sword.

6But he did not count Levi and Benjamin among them, for the king's word was detestable to Joab.

7God was displeased with this thing, and He struck Israel.

8David said to God, "I have sinned greatly in that I have done this thing. But now, please take away the guilt of Your servant, for I have acted very foolishly."

Three Choices

9The LORD spoke to Gad, David's seer, saying,

10"Go and tell David, 'Thus says the LORD: I am laying three things before you. Choose one of them, and I will do it to you.'"

11So Gad came to David and said to him, "Thus says the LORD: 'Take your choice:

12either three years of famine, or three months of being swept away before your foes while the sword of your enemies overtakes you, or three days of the sword of the LORD, plague in the land, with the messenger of the LORD destroying throughout all the territory of Israel.' Now consider what answer I shall return to the one who sent me."

13David said to Gad, "I am in great distress. Let me fall into the hand of the LORD, for His mercies are very great; but let me not fall into the hand of man."

The Messenger over Jerusalem

14So the LORD sent a plague on Israel, and seventy thousand men of Israel fell.

15God sent a messenger to Jerusalem to destroy it. But as he was destroying it, the LORD saw and relented from the evil, and said to the messenger who was destroying, "Enough! Now hold back your hand." The messenger of the LORD was standing by the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.

16David lifted up his eyes and saw the messenger of the LORD standing between earth and heaven, with a drawn sword in his hand stretched out over Jerusalem. Then David and the elders, covered in sackcloth, fell on their faces.

17David said to God, "Was it not I who ordered the people to be numbered? It is I who have sinned and done great evil. But these sheep, what have they done? O LORD my God, please let Your hand be against me and against my father's house, but not against Your people to plague them."

The Altar on the Threshing Floor

18Then the messenger of the LORD told Gad to say to David that David should go up and raise an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.

19So David went up at Gad's word, which he had spoken in the name of the LORD.

20Ornan turned and saw the messenger, and his four sons who were with him hid themselves. Ornan was threshing wheat.

21When David came to Ornan, Ornan looked and saw David, and he went out from the threshing floor and bowed down to David with his face to the ground.

22David said to Ornan, "Give me the site of the threshing floor, so that I may build on it an altar to the LORD. Give it to me at the full price, so that the plague may be held back from the people."

23Ornan said to David, "Take it, and let my lord the king do what is good in his eyes. I give the oxen for burnt offerings, the threshing sledges for the wood and the wheat for the grain offering. I give it all."

24But King David said to Ornan, "No, but I will surely buy it at the full price. I will not take what is yours for the LORD, or offer burnt offerings that cost me nothing."

25So David gave Ornan six hundred shekels of gold by weight for the site.

26David built an altar to the LORD there and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. He called on the LORD, and He answered him with fire from heaven on the altar of burnt offering.

27Then the LORD spoke to the messenger, and he put his sword back into its sheath.

28At that time, when David saw that the LORD had answered him on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite, he sacrificed there.

29For the dwelling of the LORD, which Moses had made in the wilderness, and the altar of burnt offering were at that time at the high place at Gibeon;

30but David could not go before it to inquire of God, for he was terrified because of the sword of the messenger of the LORD.

Notes

  • v1 "Satan stood up against Israel and incited David" — va-ya'amod satan, with no article. Samuel says the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and He incited David against them (2 Samuel 24:1), with the same verb, va-yasset. Satan is the word for adversary, as the messenger of the LORD took his stand in the road as an adversary against him (Numbers 22:22); in Job it has the article, ha-satan, the Adversary (Job 1:6). The Greek has diabolos, slanderer, the word the New Testament uses for the devil.

  • v3 "Why should it bring guilt on Israel?" — le-ashmah, Joab's words in Chronicles only.

  • v5 "a million one hundred thousand… four hundred and seventy thousand" — Samuel has eight hundred thousand and five hundred thousand (2 Samuel 24:9). The text keeps the Hebrew of each.

  • v6 "he did not count Levi and Benjamin… the king's word was detestable to Joab" — nit'av, from to'evah, fixed as detestable. The law had kept Levi out of the count of fighting men (Numbers 1:47–49); why Benjamin was left out is not said.

  • v12 "three years of famine" — as the text of Samuel now reads, following the Greek and Chronicles (2 Samuel 24:13).

  • v16 "standing between earth and heaven, with a drawn sword in his hand" — Balaam saw the messenger of the LORD standing in the road with his sword drawn in his hand (Numbers 22:31), and Joshua saw a man… with his sword drawn in his hand (Joshua 5:13).

  • v20 "Ornan turned and saw the messenger… Ornan was threshing wheat" — as Gideon was beating out wheat when the messenger of the LORD came (Judges 6:11). Samuel calls him Araunah (2 Samuel 24:16). The Greek has saw the king for saw the messenger.

  • vv24–25 "that cost me nothing… six hundred shekels of gold by weight for the site" — chinnam, for nothing, as in Samuel; Samuel's price is fifty shekels of silver for the threshing floor and the oxen (2 Samuel 24:24). Chronicles pays for the site, ha-maqom.

  • v26 "He answered him with fire from heaven on the altar" — as at the first offering in the tabernacle, Fire came out from before the LORD and consumed the burnt offering (Leviticus 9:24), and at Carmel (1 Kings 18:38).

  • vv29–30 "the dwelling of the LORD… at Gibeon… he was terrified because of the sword" — niv'at. The ark is in Jerusalem and the dwelling of Moses at Gibeon (16:39); David sacrifices where the messenger stood, and that site becomes the place of the house of God (22:1).

speech.text: 1 Chronicles 21
The Census
Satan stood up against Israel and incited David to number Israel.
So David said to Joab and to the commanders of the people, "Go, count Israel from Beersheba to Dan, and bring me word, so that I may know their number."

But Joab said, "May the LORD add to His people a hundred times as many as they are! My lord the king, are they not all my lord's servants? Why does my lord seek this? Why should it bring guilt on Israel?"
But the king's word prevailed against Joab. So Joab went out and went through all Israel and came back to Jerusalem.
Joab gave David the number of the people counted: all Israel was a million one hundred thousand men who drew the sword, and Judah four hundred and seventy thousand men who drew the sword.
But he did not count Levi and Benjamin among them, for the king's word was detestable to Joab.
God was displeased with this thing, and He struck Israel.
David said to God, "I have sinned greatly in that I have done this thing. But now, please take away the guilt of Your servant, for I have acted very foolishly."
Three Choices
The LORD spoke to Gad, David's seer, saying,
"Go and tell David, 'Thus says the LORD: I am laying three things before you. Choose one of them, and I will do it to you.'"
So Gad came to David and said to him, "Thus says the LORD: 'Take your choice:

either three years of famine, or three months of being swept away before your foes while the sword of your enemies overtakes you, or three days of the sword of the LORD, plague in the land, with the messenger of the LORD destroying throughout all the territory of Israel.' Now consider what answer I shall return to the one who sent me."
David said to Gad, "I am in great distress. Let me fall into the hand of the LORD, for His mercies are very great; but let me not fall into the hand of man."
The Messenger over Jerusalem
So the LORD sent a plague on Israel, and seventy thousand men of Israel fell.

God sent a messenger to Jerusalem to destroy it. But as he was destroying it, the LORD saw and relented from the evil, and said to the messenger who was destroying, "Enough! Now hold back your hand." The messenger of the LORD was standing by the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.

David lifted up his eyes and saw the messenger of the LORD standing between earth and heaven, with a drawn sword in his hand stretched out over Jerusalem. Then David and the elders, covered in sackcloth, fell on their faces.

David said to God, "Was it not I who ordered the people to be numbered? It is I who have sinned and done great evil. But these sheep, what have they done? O LORD my God, please let Your hand be against me and against my father's house, but not against Your people to plague them."
The Altar on the Threshing Floor
Then the messenger of the LORD told Gad to say to David that David should go up and raise an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
So David went up at Gad's word, which he had spoken in the name of the LORD.
Ornan turned and saw the messenger, and his four sons who were with him hid themselves. Ornan was threshing wheat.
When David came to Ornan, Ornan looked and saw David, and he went out from the threshing floor and bowed down to David with his face to the ground.
David said to Ornan, "Give me the site of the threshing floor, so that I may build on it an altar to the LORD. Give it to me at the full price, so that the plague may be held back from the people."

Ornan said to David, "Take it, and let my lord the king do what is good in his eyes. I give the oxen for burnt offerings, the threshing sledges for the wood and the wheat for the grain offering. I give it all."
But King David said to Ornan, "No, but I will surely buy it at the full price. I will not take what is yours for the LORD, or offer burnt offerings that cost me nothing."
So David gave Ornan six hundred shekels of gold by weight for the site.
David built an altar to the LORD there and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. He called on the LORD, and He answered him with fire from heaven on the altar of burnt offering.
Then the LORD spoke to the messenger, and he put his sword back into its sheath.
At that time, when David saw that the LORD had answered him on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite, he sacrificed there.
For the dwelling of the LORD, which Moses had made in the wilderness, and the altar of burnt offering were at that time at the high place at Gibeon;
but David could not go before it to inquire of God, for he was terrified because of the sword of the messenger of the LORD.
